messages:
Ravi: heads-up: running into a weird unmarshal when using function-calling + mode="json" in the SDKs. function result comes back as a JSON string instead of object.
Jo: can you paste a tiny repro?
Ravi: yup, py repro: 
```
res = client.chat.completions.create(
  model="code-alpha",
  input="make order",
  functions=[{"name":"create_order","parameters":{"type":"object"}}],
  mode="json"
)
print(res.output[0].content)
```
Ravi: printed: "{\"order_id\":42,\"status\":\"ok\"}" (note double-quoted entire JSON).
Maris: saw something similar in node last week. I think the client unwrap step for function_response expects parsed json but runtime is returning a quoted string.
Jo: any middleware affecting body encoding? auth or retry code could be reserializing.
Ravi: checked middlewares, none touched the response body. headers look fine.
sdk-bot: Created issue #2050: "SDKs: function-calling + json mode returns stringified payload"; assigned to eng-runtime.
Maris: quick workaround: call json.loads on the string when you detect leading/trailing quotes, but it's fragile.
Jo: plan: add unit tests for function-calling + mode=json across py/js, add a small opt-in helper in SDKs (e.g., client.helpers.parse_json_mode=true), then root cause in runtime and fix. update docs with migration notes.
Ravi: streaming also needs testing — stream chunks may arrive already quoted.
Maris: i'll draft the SDK helper PR and link it to #2050.
Jo: also add tests for legitimate string returns (where function should return a string) to avoid accidental double-parsing.
Ravi: thanks. uploaded repro to private repo: github.com/redwood-inference/repros/jsonmode-unmarshal
Maris: noted — QA will add cases for nested escaped quotes and arrays.
Ravi: appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
